surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the removal of ethoxy ligands from TEOS by hafnium precursors (HfCl4 or HfI4) and subsequent hydrolysis with water pulses. The reactions are described as nonhydrolytic processes where the hafnium precursor removes ethyl groups from the ethoxy ligands, leading to the formation of oxide films.
evidence: Analogous reactions have also been applied in low-temperature solgel routes to mixed porous oxides as silica-based catalysts. In order to better complete the surface reactions or increase the growth rate of dense oxide films, hydrolysis may be additionally applied after water-free reaction steps.
